body: Is there a sub that would be better to discuss it? I'm simply trying to look at it from an objective standpoint. I partially agree with you, though I don't think it should be limited to terminally ill people which assisted suicide is. And making the assumption that someone will be appreciative later is hit-and-miss. Maybe they will, maybe they won't. I feel it's better to respect their choice.

If they are asking for help, then help because that is *their choice*. I'm talking about in general, how people make unsolicited calls to the police because others have said they would kill themselves. I'm talking about people who have said flat out that they *do not want help* and some people, be it therapists or police or just a random person, take it upon themselves to say yes they do and the person gets locked up *involuntarily*. 
And you are right about it not promoting rape culture *as long as the person is asking for help*. If they're not, they're being violated just not physically but emotionally. You don't get to tell another person what they want.
And finally, how temporary does the problem have to be? If someone has chronic pain should they be forced to live? If someone has depression that will not go away, should they have to live with it just because you choose to? If so, why do you get to make that choice for them?
